rows.name: Consensus papers
rows.note: LIVE. GHOSTDAG is the consensus the Live row names. KIP-2 Proposed at kips e4ae233 says GHOSTDAG governs the current Kaspa network. https://github.com/kaspanet/kips/blob/e4ae2332117b5cb68bd6188e065ef885b6d17939/kip-0002.md Paper: Sompolinsky, Wyborski, and Zohar, ePrint 2018/104, received 2018-01-30, last of 17 revisions 2021-11-10. https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/104.pdf PDF title page 10 Nov 2021. Research mirror Ghostdag.pdf ff0ec18a is the same file, sha256 296e87afcb923b8069ed59353a2ed2440f0f42be5ac9c8623d2ffbe6c3db1a65, 1041410 bytes. https://github.com/kaspanet/research/blob/ff0ec18a6a577d534a92cbab99b7471df9a7d59c/ghostdag/Ghostdag.pdf Page 1 says GHOSTDAG was implemented as the underlying technology of Kaspa. That sentence is the 2021 paper. Section 4.2 page 7 eq. (1) is the least natural k whose f is below delta. Eq. (2) is the max of a Poisson tail of mean 2*D_max*lambda and 2c/(k+2c), with c = D_max*lambda. The same page says that second term does not vanish exponentially in k. Theorem 5, same page: the Nakamoto security threshold goes to 0 as D*lambda grows. Section 5 uses lambda=1, 2*D=7 seconds, and k=16 as an example. That example is not mainnet k. Section 6, with Figure 4 and Table 1 on page 9, records about 40 transactions per second and 458,557 transactions. Those figures are the 2021 paper. KIP-ACTIVE. KIP-14 The Crescendo Hardfork, Active, created 2025-01-21, updated 2025-03-04. https://github.com/kaspanet/kips/blob/e4ae2332117b5cb68bd6188e065ef885b6d17939/kip-0014.md It cuts target time per block from 1000 ms to 100 ms, which is 1 BPS to 10. It cites section 4.2 eq. 1 and, with D=5 and delta=0.01, sets Ghostdag K to 124 from the Poisson tail cutoff. It does not say the full f is below 0.01. Finality depth becomes 432000 blocks. The merge-depth bound becomes 36000. Coinbase maturity becomes 1000 blocks. The printed pruning expression is phi + 2M + 4KL + 2K + 2, lower bound 627258 blocks, with a suggested 30-hour round-up. Reference [3] is the Prunality PDF. The rationale names an ongoing based-ZK bridge design as anticipated demand. This hardfork is not DAGKNIGHT and not vProgs. Code at rusty-kaspa tag v2.1.0 01b532e8, and the tag object is that commit. https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16 Mainnet params use BlockrateParams for 10 BPS and crescendo activation DAA 110165000, with the comment Roughly 2025-05-05 1500 UTC. Network delay bound is 5. The tail delta is 0.01. ghostdag_k for 10 is 124. calculate_ghostdag_k returns when 1 minus the Poisson sum is below delta. It does not apply the second term of eq. (2). At mean 100, P(X>123) is 0.011244 and P(X>124) is 0.008774. The eq. (2) second term at k=124 is 100/224. The full f is not below 0.01. mergeset_size_limit is 2k when that product sits between 180 and 512, so 248 at this k. max_block_parents caps at 16. Its comment names parameterless DAGKNIGHT as a future alternative if BPS grows past 10. That comment is not a claim that DAGKNIGHT is live. pruning_depth builds the KIP-shaped lower bound and returns the larger of that bound and BPS times the pruning duration. The constants are finality 43200 seconds, merge depth 3600 seconds, and pruning 108000 seconds. At 10 BPS the bound evaluates to 627258 and the function returns 1080000. That arithmetic reads the source. It is not a consensus proof. DRAFT formula. Prunality, Sutton and Wyborski, cover July 2020, research commit 67254c9c. https://github.com/kaspanet/research/blob/67254c9c3d6d5b74ae904904b34467a199d5ee6d/prunality/Prunality.pdf Docs copy ce8c3bde (2021-07-22) is the same bytes, sha256 e7a7a35ab0c5dc95f55b28ef6e5cbf347d7b7630104be4eb7005e214e9d1336e, 201464 bytes. https://github.com/kaspanet/docs/blob/ce8c3bde44fc2cab6400a33302cc76849bf0a9a1/Reference/prunality/Prunality.pdf Page 1 sets pi = 2*phi + 4*ell*k + 2k + 2. Definition 3 on page 2 names (R-I) Objective finality. Rule 1 on page 5 says blocks in P.Past can be pruned. That pi is not the KIP-14 expression and not pruning depth 1080000. bps.rs says the lower bound is based on that PDF and on a decomposition of merge depth, rule R-I therein. That comment is not Definition 3. KIP-PROPOSED. DAGKNIGHT: Sompolinsky and Sutton, ePrint 2022/1494, received 2022-10-31, last of 2 revisions 2023-02-24. https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1494.pdf The PDF title page is 23 Feb 2023 and prints Sutton, then Sompolinsky. sha256 287ca824006d2e20d5d82fe8daf88bd21e3ba662abcec316ba026498a91384f8, 945060 bytes. The abstract says there is no a priori in-protocol latency bound, tolerance is up to 50 percent hashrate, and the protocol is an evolution of PHANTOM. Theorem 2 in section 3.2 on page 10 says Algorithm 2 is parameterless, scalable, self-stabilizing, and adaptive. Research README c923faca lists the yellow paper, Phantom Ghostdag, and Prunality. It does not list this paper. https://github.com/kaspanet/research/commit/c923faca11a49148fa7d912d27ce00197a5c5a4a Not mainnet. DRAFT. vProgs yellow paper v0.0.1, commit 12c66b138451 (2025-09-11T13:22:49Z), sha256 897196863a457368fecc4728a946abb23627ed78350d8785b89c8fa0cc983880, 387363 bytes. https://github.com/kaspanet/research/commit/12c66b1384516397c9c486c85014b38d77030fd8 The title page says DRAFT v0.0.1. The abstract says the architecture is proposed. Section 2.2 assumes a permanent static account set and does not treat creation or deletion. Section 2.4 leaves pruning of buried commitments out of scope. Section 3.1 says how ZK verification will be enabled is under consideration. Section 5.1 leaves code publication and P2P to a future version. Section 5.4 Account Creation and section 5.5 Clients Cache Pruning are left to future revisions. The abstract proposes a synchronously composable system. That proposal is not live. Kaspa does not have vProgs. KIP-ACTIVE, not that paper. rows.name: Sutton on KCC-20
rows.note:
20 Sep 2026. A properly written KCC-20 covenant is enforced by L1. KCC-20 is still a spec. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine. Same morning: KRC-20 state is off-chain interpretation, not L1. Catalog. The file is Last Call on kccs main 3fbec524 since #31 (2026-10-07T20:38:09Z), not Final. 11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement): replying to GabrielNico21 (2109049463302156773 https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773, 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton (2109305350008475670 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670, 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" 11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement): HuseyinSivridag asked (2109311950651834538 https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538, 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied (2109315001034875348 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348, 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.
in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.
(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up (2109316491417878839 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839, 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a Grok share https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983; its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. Desk reading, hedged, not his words: his answer is "not easily, no"; he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. Valid forms: native 0x00 plus 19 zero bytes, coinbase 0x01 plus 19 zero bytes, user lane of 4 namespace bytes plus 16 zero bytes with at least one nonzero byte in namespace[1..=3]. Any other shape is invalid. At most 50 distinct non-coinbase lanes in a block. Sum of tx.gas in each such lane at most 1_000_000_000. Native and reserved system lanes use tx.gas = 0. SeqCommit(B) = H_seq(SeqCommit(selected parent), SeqStateRoot(B)). Post-activation accepted_id_merkle_root is that value. KIP-15 style recurrence. The four KIP-21 files do not contain 474165565. Not desk MSG1.
